blocks.explanation:
This is the book's Example 27 repeated word for word; it is a divisibility proof.
15 is one more than 14 and 13 is one less than 14.
Plan: expand \((14 + 1)^{13}\) and \((14 - 1)^{15}\); the last terms are \(+1\) and \(-1\), which cancel.
steps:
Given: \((15)^{13} + (13)^{15}\).
To prove: it is divisible by 14.
Method: Write \(15 = 14 + 1\) and \(13 = 14 - 1\). In each binomial expansion every term except the last has a factor 14. The two last terms are \(1^{13} = 1\) and \((-1)^{15} = -1\).

Rewrite the bases
\[(15)^{13} + (13)^{15}\]
\[= (14 + 1)^{13} + (14 - 1)^{15}\]
Why: Both bases are next to the divisor 14.

Expand the first power
\[(14 + 1)^{13} = 14^{13} + {}^{13}C_1\,14^{12}\]
\[+ \dots + {}^{13}C_{12}\,14 + 1\]
\[= 14A + 1\]
Why: Every term except the last contains at least one factor 14, so their sum is \(14A\) for an integer \(A\).

Expand the second power
\[(14 - 1)^{15} = 14^{15} - {}^{15}C_1\,14^{14}\]
\[+ \dots + {}^{15}C_{14}\,14 - 1\]
\[= 14B - 1\]
Why: Signs alternate because \(x = -1\); the last term is \((-1)^{15} = -1\) because 15 is odd.

Add
\[(15)^{13} + (13)^{15} = 14A + 1 + 14B - 1\]
\[= 14(A + B)\]
Why: The \(+1\) and \(-1\) cancel, and 14 is a common factor of what is left.

Check:
\[15 + 13^3 = 15 + 2197 = 2212\]
\[2212 = 14 \times 158\]
Why: The same reasoning works for any odd power of 13 and any power of 15; this small case shows it in numbers.
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \((15)^{13} + (13)^{15} = 14(A + B)\), which is divisible by 14.
